title: Jailer 2 Posts $1.4 Million North America Premiere, Kollywood's Fourth-Biggest
excerpt: Rajinikanth's sequel passed Ponniyin Selvan's $1.11 million premiere in the US and Canada, behind only Coolie, Kabali and Leo — with Tamil audiences driving close to 90 percent of USA pre-sales.
body:
• Jailer 2 grossed $1.4 million (about Rs 13.29 crore) from North America premiere shows, according to Koimoi, making it Kollywood's fourth-biggest premiere in the territory.
  • It passed Ponniyin Selvan's $1.11 million premiere and now sits behind only Coolie ($3.04 million), Kabali ($1.92 million) and Leo ($1.86 million).
  • USA premiere pre-sales closed at $965,400 on 35,875 tickets across 1,296 shows, with the Tamil version contributing close to 90 percent, TrackTollywood reported.
  • For US and Canadian fans, the number matters more than the worldwide opening: it shows Rajinikanth's diaspora draw holding even with a muted pre-release campaign.

A North America story, not a repeat of opening day

Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 has already had its worldwide opening story. The North America premiere figure tells a different one. According to Koimoi, the film grossed $1.4 million from premiere screenings in the United States and Canada, enough for the fourth-biggest Kollywood premiere ever in the territory.

That placed it ahead of Ponniyin Selvan, which opened to $1.11 million in premieres, and behind a top three that underlines the scale of Rajinikanth's own record in the market: Coolie at $3.04 million, Kabali at $1.92 million and Leo at $1.86 million. The rest of Koimoi's top ten — The Greatest Of All Time at $1.09 million, the first Jailer at $948,000, Indian 2 at $930,000, Vettaiyan at $854,000 and Ponniyin Selvan 2 at $737,000 — shows how crowded the $1 million premiere club has become, and how difficult it still is to enter it.

"According to Koimoi , the film grossed $1.4 million from premiere screenings in the United States and Canada, enough for the fourth-biggest Kollywood premiere ever in the territory."

How the $1.4 million was built

The detailed pre-sales breakdown from TrackTollywood shows a film carried overwhelmingly by its Tamil audience. USA premiere pre-sales closed at $965,400, from 35,875 tickets across 1,296 shows in 457 theatres, at 25.2 percent average occupancy. The Tamil version accounted for $843,500 of that total, while the Telugu version contributed $121,700 after a sharp final-day rise of more than 40 percent.

By chain, Cinemark led USA pre-sales with $489,700, followed by Regal at $250,700 and AMC at $94,500. With Canada added, total North America premiere pre-sales stood at about $1.05 million before the shows, and combined premiere and opening-day pre-sales reached about $1.2 million. The final $1.4 million premiere gross therefore reflects walk-ins and last-minute buying on top of the advance — a sign that first reactions helped rather than hurt.

Strong, but below the Coolie bar

Koimoi is clear-eyed about the context: expectations had been set by Coolie, and by that standard Jailer 2 under-delivered. Its premiere finished well below $2 million, pre-release promotion was described as muted, and the sequel never generated the same advance frenzy. Judged on its own, however, $1.4 million is a strong premiere — the sequel factor alone carried it past $1 million in pre-sales before a single show had screened.

The comparison inside Rajinikanth's own filmography is instructive. Jailer 2's premiere is roughly 48 percent higher than the first Jailer's $948,000 in North America, even though the franchise sequel arrived with less hype than Coolie. For distributors, that durability — a floor that holds even in a quiet campaign — is the commercially valuable part of the result.

What diaspora audiences should watch next

Premieres measure opening-night loyalty, not staying power. The next test is the first full weekend in North America: whether word of mouth from premiere audiences expands the film beyond its core Tamil base, as pre-sales suggested it might when the Telugu version jumped on the final day, or whether it settles into a front-loaded run. Directed by Nelson Dilipkumar and produced by Sun Pictures, with a reported budget of Rs 350 crore and an ensemble including SJ Suryah, Mithun Chakraborty, Ramya Krishnan and Vidya Balan alongside major cameos, Jailer 2 needs that wider hold to convert a record premiere ranking into a record run.

For now, the headline for the diaspora is precise: fourth-biggest Kollywood premiere in North America history, ahead of Ponniyin Selvan, achieved without the hype machine that powered the three films above it.
